4. What the Service does

Talk to Me Data provides AI agents that work across the tools you use. Depending on your plan, this includes:

  • General agents that can read and act on data in tools you connect (for example Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Sheets, Slack, Notion and others), on request or on a schedule you set.
  • The Social Media Manager, which analyses public social media data for your accounts and competitors, suggests content, helps you design posts and, if you connect your accounts, publishes them to Instagram, Facebook or TikTok at the time you choose.
  • The Property Leads agent, which uses US public property records to help you find potential leads.
  • Custom agents, which we build for you after a kickoff call. Any extra terms for custom work will be agreed with you in writing.

We keep improving the Service, so features may change. If we remove a feature that is a significant part of what you pay for, we will tell you in advance and, if you are on a paid plan, you may cancel and get a pro-rata refund for the rest of your current billing period.

Some features may be labelled beta or preview. They are provided as they are, may change or be removed, and may be less reliable.

5. Plans, actions and payment

  • Plans. We offer a free Starter plan and paid plans. The current plans, prices and what each one includes (number of agents, monthly actions and other limits) are shown on our pricing and billing pages when you sign up or upgrade.
  • Actions. Most things an agent does use “actions”, for example a data pull, a tool call or a piece of AI writing. Each plan includes a monthly allowance of actions that resets on the 1st of each calendar month. Unused actions don’t carry over. When you run out, agents pause until the allowance resets or you upgrade. Because the allowance is checked before a task starts, one task in progress may finish slightly over the limit. We won’t charge you for that.
  • Billing. Paid plans are billed monthly in advance and renew automatically each month until you cancel. Payments are taken by our payment provider, Stripe. Prices are in the currency shown at checkout and include or exclude VAT as stated there.
  • Free trials and promotional offers. If we give you a free month or other offer, we’ll tell you the terms when you claim it, including when paid billing starts and how to cancel before it does.
  • Failed payments. If a payment fails, we’ll let you know and may retry it. If it still hasn’t been paid after 14 days, we may downgrade your account to the free plan.
  • Price changes. We may change our prices. We will give you at least 30 days’ notice by email before a new price applies to you. The new price will apply from your next billing period after the notice ends. If you don’t want to pay it, you can cancel before then.

6. Cancelling

Anyone can cancel at any time from the Billing page in the app (via “Manage billing”) or by emailing nas@talktomedata.com. Your paid plan stays active until the end of the billing period you’ve paid for, then your account moves to the free plan. We don’t refund part-used billing periods, except as set out in this section or where the law requires it.

Consumers: your 14-day right to cancel. If you are a consumer, you have a legal right to cancel a paid subscription within 14 days of the day you first buy it, without giving a reason. Because the Service starts straight away, when you subscribe you ask us to start providing it during that 14-day period. If you then cancel within the 14 days, we will refund what you paid minus a proportionate amount for the Service provided up to the day you told us you were cancelling. To cancel, email nas@talktomedata.com or use the Billing page. We will refund you within 14 days of your cancellation, using the payment method you used.

7. Connecting your tools and social media accounts

  • When you connect a tool or social media account, you authorise us to access it and take the actions you ask for (or schedule) on your behalf, within the permissions you approved.
  • You must only connect accounts you own or are authorised to use.
  • You remain responsible for your use of those tools and platforms, and must follow their terms. These include the Instagram Terms of Use, Meta’s Terms, TikTok’s Terms of Service, and Google’s terms.
  • YouTube. The Social Media Manager uses YouTube API Services. By using its YouTube features, you agree to be bound by the YouTube Terms of Service. See also the Google Privacy Policy.
  • Publishing. We only publish a post when you choose “Post now” or schedule it to be posted automatically. You are responsible for reviewing every post before it is published, including any AI-generated text or images, and for any disclosures the platform or law requires (for example, marking paid partnerships or ads).
  • Platforms can change or restrict their APIs, suspend our access, or reject posts at any time. We will tell you if a post fails, but we are not responsible for a platform’s decisions or outages.
  • You can disconnect any tool or account at any time in the app.

8. AI-generated content

  • Our agents use AI models to analyse data and produce text, images and suggestions (“Output”). AI Output can be inaccurate, incomplete or out of date, and similar Output may be given to other users.
  • Check Output before you rely on it or share it, especially for anything with legal, financial or reputational consequences. The Service does not give professional (legal, financial, tax or property) advice.
  • Subject to these terms, you own the Output created for you, as far as the law allows, and you can use it for any lawful purpose. We don’t claim ownership of it.

9. Property Leads

  • Property Leads uses public records from US local government sources. These records may contain errors or be out of date, and we don’t guarantee their accuracy or completeness.
  • If you use the Service to contact property owners, you are responsible for following all laws that apply to you. For US contacts, these include telemarketing and do-not-call rules, anti-spam laws and fair housing laws.
  • If you upload contact lists, you confirm you have the right to share them with us for matching. For that data we act as your processor (see section 12).

12. Data protection (for business customers)

When our agents process personal data contained in Your Content on your behalf (for example emails or contacts), you are the controller and we are your processor. For that processing, we will:

  • process the data only on your documented instructions (these terms and your use of the Service) unless the law requires otherwise;
  • make sure anyone we authorise to process it is bound by confidentiality;
  • take appropriate technical and organisational security measures;
  • only use the sub-processors listed in our Privacy Policy. We will tell you about any new sub-processor in advance, and you may object. If we can’t resolve your objection, you may cancel and get a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. We will put data protection terms in place with every sub-processor that are at least as protective as these;
  • only transfer the data outside the UK with appropriate safeguards;
  • help you respond to requests from people exercising their data rights, and with security, breach notification, impact assessments and consultations with the ICO, taking into account the nature of the processing;
  • notify you without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting that data;
  • delete or return the data when you close your account, unless the law requires us to keep it; and
  • give you the information you reasonably need to show compliance with Article 28 of the UK GDPR, and allow for and contribute to reasonable audits on reasonable notice.

The subject matter is providing the Service. The duration is the life of your account. The data types and people concerned depend on what you connect and upload.
